questions.question: Which of the following is a way hotels maintain the security of guests' credit card data:

options.A: Storing card numbers in an open spreadsheet
options.D: Writing card numbers on sticky notes

questions.explanation: Encrypting payment information. Encryption scrambles payment data so it can't be read if intercepted. Writing numbers down, sending them by email, or storing them in an unprotected spreadsheet makes them easy to steal and violates payment security standards.

performanceIndicator.text: Maintain data security

questions.question: Which of the following is an environmental change that a hospitality business should track:

options.A: The brand of pens at the front desk
options.B: The color of its own uniforms
options.C: The number of chairs in its lobby

questions.explanation: New regulations on short-term rentals. Changes outside the business, such as new laws, technology, economic shifts, and guest trends, can affect demand and operations. Uniform colors, chairs, and pens are internal details that the business already controls.

performanceIndicator.text: Track environmental changes that impact hospitality and tourism (e.g., technological changes, guest trends, economic changes, regulatory changes)

questions.question: A small bed-and-breakfast is deciding whether to accept credit cards. Which consideration is most important?

options.A: How many employees know about credit history
options.B: Whether guests prefer the color of the card reader
options.C: Whether the owner personally uses credit cards
options.D: The cost of processing fees compared with the extra sales

questions.explanation: The cost of processing fees compared with the extra sales. The business must weigh fees and equipment costs against the bookings it may gain from guests who expect to pay by card. The card reader's color, employees' knowledge of credit history, and the owner's own habits aren't key business considerations.

performanceIndicator.text: Discuss considerations in accepting credit-card payments

questions.question: A tour guide leading a group of international visitors notices several of them look confused by her jokes and fast speech. What should she do?

options.A: Ask them to find a different tour
options.B: Tell more jokes to lighten the mood

questions.explanation: Speak more slowly and simply. Adapting by slowing down and choosing clear language helps visitors whose first language is different understand the tour. More jokes, ignoring confusion, or sending them away would make the experience worse.

performanceIndicator.text: Adapt communication to the cultural and social differences among clients

questions.question: When the economy is strong and incomes are rising, the hospitality and tourism industry usually
questions.explanation: Sees more travel spending. Travel and dining out are largely discretionary purchases, so people spend more on them when they feel financially secure. A strong economy tends to increase, not decrease, demand, hiring, and hotel openings.

performanceIndicator.text: Explain the relationship between the economy and hospitality and tourism

questions.question: A diner at Riverside Grill begins choking and cannot speak. What should a trained employee do first?

options.A: Call for help and give first aid
options.B: Ask the diner to leave the restaurant
options.C: Wait for the diner's friends to help
options.D: Offer the diner a glass of water

questions.explanation: Call for help and give first aid. Choking is a life-threatening emergency. A trained employee should have someone call 911 and immediately begin first-aid techniques such as abdominal thrusts. Water can make choking worse, asking the diner to leave is dangerous, and waiting wastes critical time.

performanceIndicator.text: Handle emergency situations in hospitality and tourism

questions.question: Why is consistent service difficult to achieve in the hospitality industry?

options.B: Every guest has exactly the same expectations
options.C: Quality depends on many employees and situations

questions.explanation: Quality depends on many employees and situations. Guests interact with many employees, each with different skills and moods, and conditions change constantly, which makes consistency a challenge. Guests' expectations vary, businesses do train employees, and most hospitality services are delivered by people.

performanceIndicator.text: Describe customer-service challenges in the hospitality and tourism industry

questions.question: The marketing team at Pinewood Lodge wants to know which states its repeat guests come from. Which database function would help most?

options.A: Deleting guests who stayed only once
options.B: A query grouping repeat guests by state
options.C: Changing the font of the database

questions.explanation: A query grouping repeat guests by state. A query can filter repeat guests and group them by state, giving the team a quick summary. Changing fonts doesn't analyze anything, deleting guests loses valuable data, and printing the full list makes the analysis slower.

performanceIndicator.text: Use database for information analysis

questions.question: Tracking invoices helps a hospitality business

options.B: decide which menu items to promote.
options.D: pay bills on time and correctly.

questions.explanation: Pay bills on time and correctly. Keeping track of invoices shows what is owed, when it is due, and whether the charges match what was ordered, which avoids late fees and overpayments. Menu promotion, staff scheduling, and web design are not part of invoice tracking.

performanceIndicator.text: Track invoices

questions.question: Which of the following is a way for a student to gain work experience in hospitality:

options.C: Watching online videos about travel careers

questions.explanation: Volunteering at a community festival. Volunteering at events gives students hands-on experience in guest service, teamwork, and event operations that employers value. Watching videos, reading reviews, and taking photos may build interest but don't provide work experience.

performanceIndicator.text: Describe techniques for obtaining work experience (e.g., volunteer activities, internships)

questions.question: The manager of Copper Kettle Diner exports last month's transactions to a spreadsheet, sorts them by menu item, and totals the quantity sold to find the five top-selling dishes. This is an example of a(n)
questions.explanation: Basic data mining technique. Sorting and summarizing transaction data reveals patterns such as best-sellers, a basic form of data mining. An inventory count tallies stock on hand, a job analysis studies a position's duties, and a sales promotion is a short-term incentive.

performanceIndicator.text: Demonstrate basic data mining techniques

questions.question: Two guests at a hotel pool argue over lounge chairs that one of them reserved with towels hours earlier. The pool attendant should

options.A: take one guest's side without listening.
options.B: close the pool for the day.
options.C: ignore the argument and hope it ends on its own.
options.D: explain the chair policy and help both find seats.

questions.explanation: Explain the chair policy and help both find seats. Explaining the policy fairly and finding a solution for both guests resolves the conflict without favoritism. Ignoring it lets the problem escalate, taking sides creates more anger, and closing the pool punishes everyone.

performanceIndicator.text: Resolve hospitality and tourism related conflicts for customers

questions.question: Which of the following should a hotel purchasing manager consider when evaluating a linen-supply vendor:

options.A: Whether the vendor's office is attractive
options.B: How many social media followers the vendor has

questions.explanation: Quality, price, and delivery reliability. Vendors should be judged on whether their products meet quality standards, are fairly priced, and arrive on time. Personal preferences, social media popularity, and office appearance don't show whether a vendor will meet the hotel's needs.

performanceIndicator.text: Evaluate vendors' goods and services

questions.question: Which of the following is an environmental sustainability issue in the hospitality industry:

options.B: The number of guest loyalty members

questions.explanation: Water use in hotel laundries. Hotels use large amounts of water for laundry, pools, and landscaping, so water conservation is a major sustainability issue. Loyalty programs, key design, and break schedules aren't environmental issues.

performanceIndicator.text: Identify environmental sustainability issues in hospitality and tourism

questions.question: A hotel sells rooms through its own website, a global booking service, and corporate travel agents. Why does it use multiple distribution channels?

options.B: To raise the cost of each booking

questions.explanation: To reach more potential guests. Different travelers book in different ways, so using several channels widens the hotel's reach. Some channels charge commissions, which the hotel accepts to gain bookings. The goal isn't to raise costs or confuse competitors.

performanceIndicator.text: Explain the nature and scope of distribution

questions.question: Many travelers now seek trips where they can cook with local families, learn traditional crafts, or volunteer in the community. This trend is known as
questions.explanation: Experiential travel. Experiential travel focuses on authentic, hands-on activities that connect travelers with local people and culture. Mass tourism moves large numbers of people to popular sites, business travel is done for work, and package tours bundle standard transportation and lodging.

performanceIndicator.text: Describe current issues and trends in the hospitality and tourism industry

questions.question: Groupware applications help hospitality teams by

options.A: letting members share files in one place.

questions.explanation: Letting members share files in one place. Collaborative software lets employees share calendars, documents, and messages, which improves coordination across shifts and departments. It supports, but doesn't replace, meetings and managers, and it has nothing to do with cooking.

performanceIndicator.text: Demonstrate collaborative/groupware applications

questions.question: The average number of guests a restaurant serves per night is an example of a
questions.explanation: Measure of central tendency. Measures of central tendency, such as the mean, median, and mode, describe the typical value in a data set. Measures of variation show how spread out the data are, sampling error is the difference between a sample and the population, and qualitative findings describe non-numerical information.

performanceIndicator.text: Explain the use of descriptive statistics in business decision making

questions.question: Guest recovery refers to

options.B: fixing a service failure to regain satisfaction.
options.C: finding guests who left items behind.
options.D: bringing guests back to the lobby after an evacuation.

questions.explanation: Fixing a service failure to regain satisfaction. Guest recovery is how a business responds when something goes wrong. It typically involves listening, apologizing, solving the problem, and sometimes offering compensation. It isn't about lost-and-found items, bill collection, or evacuations.

performanceIndicator.text: Explain the nature of guest recovery

questions.question: A restaurant's mean check average is $42, but the median is $30. What does this suggest?

options.A: A few large checks are raising the mean

questions.explanation: A few large checks are raising the mean. When the mean is well above the median, a few unusually high values pull the average up. The median shows that half of checks are $30 or less, so most are not above $42. The numbers aren't necessarily wrong, and they don't show the range.

performanceIndicator.text: Interpret descriptive statistics for business decision making

questions.question: Which of the following should a restaurant do first when selecting a vendor:

options.A: Identify its needs and the standards products must meet
options.B: Choose the vendor with the most attractive website
options.C: Sign a contract with the first vendor that calls
options.D: Ask employees to choose their favorite vendor

questions.explanation: Identify its needs and the standards products must meet. Knowing exactly what the restaurant needs, including quality, quantity, and delivery, allows it to compare vendors fairly. Attractive websites, first contacts, and personal favorites don't ensure a vendor will meet those needs.

performanceIndicator.text: Select vendors

questions.question: Which of the following is a crucial element of a quality culture in a hospitality business?
questions.explanation: Leaders who support continuous improvement. Leadership commitment encourages employees to seek better ways of working and to speak up about problems. Punishing those who report problems, hiding standards, and ignoring feedback discourage quality.

performanceIndicator.text: Describe crucial elements of a quality culture

questions.question: Consensus building is a process in which

options.C: a group seeks a decision all can support.
options.D: the leader makes every decision alone.

questions.explanation: A group seeks a decision all can support. Consensus building involves discussing ideas, addressing concerns, and finding a solution everyone can accept, even if it isn't anyone's first choice. Leader-only decisions, ignoring minority views, and votes without discussion don't build consensus.

performanceIndicator.text: Use consensus-building skills

questions.question: Rohan is preparing slides about hotel occupancy trends for managers. Which slide design choice is most effective?

options.A: A dark background with dark text
options.B: A simple chart with a clear title
options.D: A slide with ten bullet points in small type

questions.explanation: A simple chart with a clear title. A simple chart with a clear title communicates the trend quickly. Many small bullet points overwhelm viewers, constant animation distracts, and dark text on a dark background is hard to read.

performanceIndicator.text: Prepare and use presentation software to aid in making oral reports

questions.question: Which of the following should an employee do when taking a telephone order for a catered event:

options.A: Repeat the order back to the customer to confirm it
options.B: Hang up as soon as the customer names the first item

questions.explanation: Repeat the order back to the customer to confirm it. Reading the order back lets the customer catch any mistakes before the food is prepared. Hanging up early, guessing details, and skipping special requests lead to incorrect orders and unhappy customers.

performanceIndicator.text: Process telephone orders in hospitality and tourism

questions.question: A customer-service challenge unique to many hospitality businesses is that

options.B: products can be returned for a full refund.
options.C: service is produced and used at once.
options.D: demand is the same every day of the year.

questions.explanation: Service is produced and used at once. Because a meal or hotel stay is delivered while the guest experiences it, mistakes can't be fixed before the guest sees them. Hospitality experiences can't be returned, guests interact with employees constantly, and demand varies widely by season and day.

performanceIndicator.text: Describe customer-service challenges in the hospitality and tourism industry

questions.question: Data mining is the process of

options.A: printing reports for managers each month.
options.B: finding patterns in large amounts of data.

questions.explanation: Finding patterns in large amounts of data. Data mining uses software to search large data sets for trends and relationships that help businesses make decisions. Data entry, deleting files, and printing reports are routine tasks that don't uncover patterns.

performanceIndicator.text: Describe data mining tools and techniques

questions.question: Which of the following should a writer do first when revising a business document:

options.B: Add as many words as possible
options.C: Check that the message is clear and organized
options.D: Change the font to something decorative

questions.explanation: Check that the message is clear and organized. Revision focuses on big-picture issues first, such as clarity, organization, and completeness, before smaller fixes like grammar. Decorative fonts, extra words, and removing the main point make documents less effective.

performanceIndicator.text: Edit and revise written work consistent with professional standards

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of primary market information for a restaurant:

options.A: Census data about the city's population
options.C: Comment cards filled out by its diners
options.D: A newspaper article about food trends

questions.explanation: Comment cards filled out by its diners. Comment cards collect opinions directly from the restaurant's own customers, so they are primary information. Industry reports, census data, and news articles were produced by others and are secondary sources.

performanceIndicator.text: Explain types of primary hospitality and tourism market information

questions.question: The manager of Seabreeze Café receives an invoice for 40 cases of lettuce, but the delivery receipt shows only 30 cases arrived. What should the manager do?

options.A: Pay the full invoice to keep the vendor happy
options.B: Order 10 more cases from another vendor
options.C: Ask the vendor to correct the invoice

questions.explanation: Ask the vendor to correct the invoice. Comparing invoices with delivery records catches billing errors. The manager should ask the vendor to correct the invoice so the café pays only for what it received. Paying for undelivered goods wastes money, discarding the invoice causes problems later, and ordering elsewhere doesn't fix the billing error.

performanceIndicator.text: Track invoices

questions.question: The Tanaka family chose a lakeside resort because it offered kids' activities, a short drive from home, and good reviews from other parents. Which motivating factors influenced their choice?
questions.explanation: Convenience and family-friendly amenities. The family focused on how easy the trip would be and what activities their children could enjoy, so convenience and family amenities were the main motivators. Meeting facilities, luxury shopping, and adult nightlife were not part of their decision.

performanceIndicator.text: Explain factors that motivate people to choose a hospitality and tourism site

questions.question: A cruise line creates separate promotions for college students on spring break and for retirees who want longer, quieter voyages. The cruise line is segmenting its market by
questions.explanation: Age and life stage. College students and retirees differ mainly in age and stage of life, which shapes what they want from a cruise. The promotions are not based on where customers live, the size of the ship, or fuel prices.

performanceIndicator.text: Identify ways to segment hospitality and tourism markets

questions.question: A restaurant's card processor charges 2.5% of each transaction plus $0.10. What is the processing cost on a $60 meal?
questions.explanation: $1.60. The percentage fee is 2.5% x $60 = $1.50, and adding the $0.10 transaction fee gives $1.60. $1.50 leaves out the flat fee, $2.50 treats the percentage as a dollar amount, and $6.10 uses 10% instead of 2.5%.

performanceIndicator.text: Calculate credit-card processing costs

questions.question: Evaluating project results involves

options.A: choosing team members for the project.
options.C: comparing results with the original goals.
options.D: starting a new project before the current one ends.

questions.explanation: Comparing results with the original goals. Evaluation looks back at outcomes to see whether goals, budget, and schedule were met, and what lessons can improve future projects. Starting new projects, choosing team members, and budgeting happen before or during a project.

performanceIndicator.text: Evaluate project results

questions.question: Which of the following is a right that hotel guests generally have:
questions.explanation: Privacy in their rooms. Guests have a reasonable expectation of privacy in their rooms, and staff may enter only for legitimate reasons. Free unlimited room service, other guests' rooms, and employee areas are not guest rights.

performanceIndicator.text: Describe the rights of customers in the hospitality and tourism industry

questions.question: A city requires all hotels to collect an extra tax on room charges to fund tourism promotion. This is an example of
questions.explanation: A government regulation. Taxes required by law, such as lodging or occupancy taxes, are government regulations that hotels must follow. Voluntary standards, private policies, and service guidelines are chosen by businesses or associations rather than imposed by government.

performanceIndicator.text: Explain the nature of regulations affecting the hospitality and tourism industry

questions.question: Which of the following should an employee do first when recommending hospitality services to a guest:

options.A: Suggest the most expensive option available
options.B: Determine the guest's needs and interests
options.C: List every service the business offers
options.D: Recommend whatever he or she personally enjoys

questions.explanation: Determine the guest's needs and interests. Recommendations are most helpful when they match what the guest wants, so the employee should ask questions and listen first. Pushing expensive options, overwhelming the guest with every service, or relying on personal taste may not meet the guest's needs.

performanceIndicator.text: Recommend hospitality and tourism services

questions.question: Which of the following should a presenter do when using presentation software for an oral report:

options.A: Use slides with key points and visuals
options.B: Read every word from the slides
options.C: Use many different fonts and colors on each slide
options.D: Fill each slide with as much text as possible

questions.explanation: Use slides with key points and visuals. Slides should support the speaker, highlighting main points and helpful visuals. Reading slides word for word bores the audience, crowded text is hard to read, and too many fonts and colors are distracting.

performanceIndicator.text: Prepare and use presentation software to aid in making oral reports

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of following established security procedures in a hotel:

options.C: Checking ID before issuing a new room key
options.D: Propping open employee entrances for convenience

questions.explanation: Checking ID before issuing a new room key. Verifying identity before giving out keys prevents unauthorized people from entering guest rooms. Propping doors, sharing codes, and leaving cash unprotected create security risks.

performanceIndicator.text: Follow established security procedures/policies

questions.question: The Bayside Hotel and Coastal Airways agree that guests who stay three nights at the hotel will earn 1,500 bonus miles on the airline, and the airline will feature the hotel in its in-flight magazine. The two companies are using
questions.explanation: Cross-promotion. Cross-promotion occurs when two businesses join forces to promote each other's products, reaching both companies' customers. Personal selling involves one-on-one sales contact, publicity is unpaid media coverage, and public service ads promote social causes.

performanceIndicator.text: Explain promotional methods used by the hospitality and tourism industry

questions.question: Monitoring hospitality sales data helps managers
questions.explanation: Spot trends and adjust plans. Sales data shows which days, products, or services are performing well or poorly, so managers can respond with better schedules, prices, or marketing. It supports decision making and works alongside inventory tracking and feedback.

performanceIndicator.text: Monitor hospitality and tourism sales data

questions.question: A front desk clerk at Bayview Hotel receives an email that appears to be from the hotel's IT department asking her to enter her password on a website. What should she do?

options.A: Forward the email to all coworkers
options.B: Check with IT before clicking anything
options.D: Reply with her password to save time

questions.explanation: Check with IT before clicking anything. This is a common phishing attempt. IT departments rarely ask for passwords by email. Confirming through a known phone number or contact protects the hotel's systems. Entering or replying with her password could give hackers access, and forwarding the email spreads the risk.

performanceIndicator.text: Maintain data security

questions.question: A collection of related fields about one guest, such as name, address, and room number, is called a
questions.explanation: Record. A record contains all the fields for one item or person. A table holds many records, a macro automates tasks, and a chart displays data visually.

performanceIndicator.text: Demonstrate basic database applications

questions.question: A resort wants to invite guests who have stayed during the winter holidays for the past three years to an exclusive early-booking offer. How should it find these guests?

options.A: Ask employees to remember regular guests
options.B: Search its database for those stay dates
options.C: Post the offer on a billboard
options.D: Mail the offer to every household in the state

questions.explanation: Search its database for those stay dates. Searching the database by stay dates quickly produces an accurate list of the right guests. Memory is unreliable, and billboards and statewide mailings reach many people who don't qualify.

performanceIndicator.text: Obtain business information from customer databases

questions.question: A café's weekly report shows that iced drink sales drop by half on rainy days. How might the manager use this information?

options.A: Order fewer iced-drink supplies when rain is forecast
options.C: Ignore the data because weather can't be controlled
options.D: Close the café on rainy days

questions.explanation: Order fewer iced-drink supplies when rain is forecast. Knowing how weather affects sales helps the manager plan inventory and reduce waste. Dropping iced drinks or closing loses sales on good days, and ignoring the data wastes useful information.

performanceIndicator.text: Monitor hospitality and tourism sales data

questions.question: A competitive advantage is

options.A: the amount of money a business owes.
options.C: the minimum price a business can charge.
options.D: a promotion that every competitor also offers.

questions.explanation: A valued strength competitors lack. A competitive advantage gives customers a reason to choose one business over another, such as a unique location or exceptional service. Debt, common promotions, and minimum prices don't set a business apart.

performanceIndicator.text: Identify product's/service's competitive advantage

questions.question: Which of the following is a concern associated with data mining:
questions.explanation: Protecting customers' privacy. Data mining uses large amounts of personal information, so businesses must protect privacy and use data responsibly. Finding patterns, improving decisions, and understanding preferences are the benefits of data mining, not concerns.

performanceIndicator.text: Discuss the nature of data mining

questions.question: The hospitality and tourism industry includes businesses in
questions.explanation: Lodging, food, travel, and recreation. Hospitality and tourism covers hotels, restaurants, transportation, attractions, and events that serve travelers and guests. Banking and insurance are part of finance, farming and mining are natural resource industries, and car manufacturing is production.

performanceIndicator.text: Describe the nature of the hospitality and tourism industry

questions.question: An event-planning team in three cities needs to update one guest list at the same time. Which tool would work best?

options.A: Separate printed copies for each planner

questions.explanation: A shared online spreadsheet. A shared online spreadsheet lets everyone view and edit the latest version at once, preventing conflicting copies. Printed copies quickly fall out of date, and voicemail and fax can't support real-time editing.

performanceIndicator.text: Demonstrate collaborative/groupware applications

questions.question: Carmen is searching for festivals in Portland, Maine, but keeps getting results about Portland, Oregon. Which search would help most?

options.C: Festivals in the city of Portland

questions.explanation: Portland Maine festivals -Oregon. Adding "Maine" and using a minus sign to exclude "Oregon" filters out unwanted results. A search for festivals in Portland alone is too broad, adding "Oregon" brings in the wrong city, and "fun things" is vague.

performanceIndicator.text: Demonstrate basic web-search skills
